data.title: Saudi Arabia Calls for Sustainable Regional Security Architecture Based on Mutual Guarantees at Mediterranean Dialogues
data.content:
Naples, November 21, 2026, SPA -- Advisor and Special Envoy of the Minister of Foreign Affairs for Negotiations and Peace Efforts Manal Radwan took part in a session titled "Redefining Security: Iran, the Straits, and the Future of the Regional Order" at the Mediterranean Dialogues (MED) conference in Naples, Italy.
    Radwan said the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia continues to pursue an approach combining containment, deterrence, and dialogue, and that its defense of its own security, the security and stability of the Gulf, and the vital waterways of the Strait of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab Strait serves the interests of the whole world.
    She called for a sustainable regional security architecture in which each state's security is linked to that of its neighbors and not achieved at another's expense, founded on mutual security guarantees, so that the end of one round of conflict does not merely set the stage for a more violent one.
    Temporary arrangements will not work unless they are aligned with long-term strategic frameworks, Radwan said. Dealing with armed groups outside state control requires a political vision, not only a security one, that addresses the local causes of their emergence and their links to the external parties that support and exploit them.
    She said Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) member states are united in their objectives and that their roles should complement one another in supporting mediation, de-escalation, and the prevention of a new war, paving the way for confidence-building. Regional dialogue and international stability are closely linked, she added, and there is no place in the region for any hegemonic power.
    On Yemen, Radwan said the war is at its core an intra-Yemeni conflict, and the Kingdom supports a resolution through political and economic tracks in line with the UN-led roadmap.
    She warned that merely managing the region's crises for years to come without addressing their root causes could have catastrophic consequences for all, and called for collective action to seize the current opportunity for a comprehensive and sustainable solution that serves all parties, includes the realization of a Palestinian state, fosters regional integration, and keeps pace with global geostrategic shifts.
    -- SPA
